statement.text:
Let $p$ be a prime. Let $G$ be a transitive subgroup of the group of finitary permutations $\operatorname{FSym}(\Omega)$ of a set $\Omega$, let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$, and let $S$ be a transitive Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$.

(a) Is it true that $S\cap N$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $N$?

(b) Is it true that $SN/N$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G/N$?

(c) Are any two transitive Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$ locally conjugate in $G$?

Two subgroups $X,Y$ of a group $G$ are said to be locally conjugate if there is a locally inner automorphism $\phi$ of $G$ such that $X^\phi=Y$. An automorphism $\phi$ of $G$ is said to be locally inner if for every finite subset $A\subseteq G$ there is an element $g=g(A)\in G$ such that $a^\phi=g^{-1}ag$ for all $a\in A$.
